babs.2: A man bathing together with his wife
babs.3: Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like
babs.4: One who poured water over his head three times
babs.6: One who began with a vessel (ḥilāb) or perfume when bathing
babs.7: Rinsing mouth and nose in janāba
babs.8: May the junub put his hand in the vessel before washing it?
babs.10: One who poured with his right hand onto his left in the bath
babs.11: When one has intercourse and repeats it, and one who went round his wives with a single bath
babs.12: Washing off madhy and ablution because of it
babs.13: One who perfumed himself, then bathed, and the trace of perfume remained
babs.14: Running the fingers through the hair until one thinks the skin is moistened, then pouring water over it
babs.15: One who performed ablution in janāba and then washed the rest of his body
babs.16: When one remembers in the mosque that one is junub: he goes out as he is and does not perform tayammum
babs.17: Shaking the hands after bathing from janāba
babs.18: One who began with the right side of his head in the bath
babs.19: One who bathed naked alone in seclusion, and one who covered himself – covering is better
babs.20: Covering oneself when bathing in front of people
babs.21: When a woman has a wet dream
babs.22: The sweat of the junub, and that the Muslim does not become impure
babs.23: The junub going out and walking in the market and elsewhere
babs.24: The junub staying in the house if he performed ablution before bathing
babs.26: The junub performs ablution and then sleeps
babs.27: When the two circumcised parts meet
babs.28: Washing what touches one from the woman's private part

248.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he began by washing his hands, then performed ablution as for prayer, then put his fingers into the water and ran them through the roots of his hair, then poured three handfuls over his head with his hands, then let the water flow over all his skin.”
248.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution before the bath.” ʿĀʾisha describes the sequence: first washing the hands, then the prayer ablution, then running the fingers through the roots of the hair, pouring water three times over the head, and finally pouring water over the whole skin. The chain runs through ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf, Mālik, Hishām and his father to ʿĀʾisha.

249.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, she said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed his ablution for prayer except for his feet, and washed his private part and whatever filth had touched him, then poured water over himself, then moved aside and washed his feet. This was his bath from janāba.”
249.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution before the bath.” Maymūna describes a sequence: prayer ablution without the feet, washing the private part and the filth, pouring water over himself, then moving aside and washing the feet. The wording stresses that this was his bath from janāba.

250.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, from a bowl called al-Faraq.”
250.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man bathing together with his wife.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she and the Prophet bathed from the same vessel, a bowl called al-Faraq. The text gives no further detail on the size of the bowl.

251.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd aṣ-Ṣamad narrated to me, he said: Shuʿba narrated to me, he said: Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū Salama say: “I and ʿĀʾisha’s brother went in to ʿĀʾisha, and her brother asked her about the bathing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She called for a vessel of about a ṣāʿ, bathed and poured water over her head, with a screen between us and her.” Abū ʿAbdallāh said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī said, from Shuʿba: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”
251.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” When her brother asks about the bathing of the Prophet, ʿĀʾisha has a vessel of about a ṣāʿ brought and bathes behind a screen. Abū ʿAbdallāh (al-Bukhārī) adds the wording of Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”

252.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us: “He was with Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, he and his father, and with him were some people. They asked him about the bath, and he said: A ṣāʿ is enough for you. A man said: It is not enough for me. Jābir said: It was enough for one who had more hair than you and was better than you. Then he led us in prayer in one garment.”
252.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” Asked about the bath, Jābir says a ṣāʿ is enough. To a man for whom it is not enough, he replies that it was enough for one who had more hair and was better; the wording does not name him explicitly. He then led the prayer in one garment.

253.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Maymūna used to bathe from one vessel.” And Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī said, from Shuʿba: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”
253.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” The wording reports that the Prophet and Maymūna bathed from one vessel. The statement “the measure of a ṣāʿ” is added here by Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī through Shuʿba.

254.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad narrated to me, he said: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I pour water over my head three times.” And he gestured with both his hands.
254.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” The Prophet says he pours water over his head three times and gestures with both hands. The chain runs through Abū Nuʿaym, Zuhayr, Abū Isḥāq and Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad to Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.

255.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Mukhawwal ibn Rāshid, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pour water over his head three times.”
255.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” Jābir reports briefly that the Prophet poured water over his head three times. The chain runs through Muḥammad ibn Bashshār, Ghundar, Shuʿba, Mukhawwal and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī to Jābir.

256.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā ibn Sām narrated to us: Abū Jaʿfar narrated to me, he said: Jābir said to me: “Your cousin came to me” – alluding to al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya – “he said: How is the bath from janāba? I said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would take three handfuls and pour them over his head, then pour water over the rest of his body. Al-Ḥasan said to me: I am a man with a lot of hair. I said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had more hair than you.”
256.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” Jābir describes to the questioner that the Prophet poured three handfuls over his head and then over the rest of his body. To the objection that he has a lot of hair, Jābir replies that the Prophet had more.

257.matn: Mūsā narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna said: “I set out water for the bath for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He washed his hands two or three times, then poured on his left and washed his private parts, then rubbed his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and hands, then poured water over his body, then moved from his place and washed his feet.”
257.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing once.” Maymūna describes: washing the hands, washing the private parts with the left hand, rubbing the hand on the ground, rinsing mouth and nose, washing face and hands, pouring water over the body, and finally moving aside and washing the feet. The wording leaves open whether the hands were washed two or three times.

258.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Ḥanẓala, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he called for something like the ḥilāb, took some with his hand, began with the right side of his head, then the left, and went over his head with both hands.”
258.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who began with a vessel (ḥilāb) or perfume when bathing.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet called for something like the ḥilāb and began with the right side of the head, then the left. The text does not explain the word ḥilāb.

259.matn: ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said: Sālim narrated to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna narrated to us, she said: “I poured out bath water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He poured with his right hand over his left and washed both, then washed his private part, then struck his hand on the ground and rubbed it with soil, then washed it, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and poured water over his head, then moved aside and washed his feet. Then a towel was brought to him, and he did not shake himself with it.”
259.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Rinsing mouth and nose in janāba.” Maymūna describes the sequence of the bath: hands, private part, rubbing the hand on soil, rinsing mouth and nose, face, head, then the feet. At the end a towel is brought, and he did not shake himself with it.

260.matn: al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba. He washed his private part with his hand, then rubbed it on the wall, then washed it, then performed his ablution for prayer, and when he finished his bath he washed his feet.”
260.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Rinsing mouth and nose in janāba.” Maymūna describes: washing the private part with the hand, rubbing the hand on the wall and washing it, then the prayer ablution and finally the feet. Unlike the previous hadith, the hand is rubbed here on the wall instead of the ground.

261.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us: Aflaḥ informed us, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, our hands alternating in it.”
261.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “May the junub put his hand in the vessel before washing it?” ʿĀʾisha reports that she and the Prophet bathed from one vessel, their hands going into it in turn. The chain runs through ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama, Aflaḥ and al-Qāsim to ʿĀʾisha.

262.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he washed his hand.”
262.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter, “May the junub put his hand in the vessel before washing it?” The wording is short: when the Prophet bathed from janāba, he first washed his hand. The text says nothing about number or details.

263.matn: Abū l-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel from janāba.” And from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, the same.
263.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. ʿĀʾisha reports that she and the Prophet bathed from janāba from one vessel. At the end al-Bukhārī adds a second chain through ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim and his father with the same wording.

264.matn: Abū l-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Jabr, he said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of his wives used to bathe from one vessel.” Muslim and Wahb added from Shuʿba: “from janāba.”
264.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Anas reports that the Prophet and one of his wives bathed from one vessel. Muslim and Wahb add “from janāba” through Shuʿba; the wife’s name is not given.

265.matn: Muḥammad ibn Maḥbūb narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna said: “I set out water for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe with. He poured it over his hands and washed them twice, twice, or three times, then poured with his right hand over his left and washed his private parts, then rubbed his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and his hands, and washed his head three times, then poured water over his body, then moved away from his place and washed his feet.”
265.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Separating the bath and ablution.” Maymūna describes that the Prophet washed his feet only at the end, after moving aside. The wording leaves open whether the hands were washed twice or three times.

266.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith, she said: “I set out bathing water for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and screened him. He poured on his hand and washed it once or twice – Sulaymān said: I do not know whether he mentioned the third or not. Then he poured with his right on his left and washed his private part, then rubbed his hand on the ground or on the wall, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and hands and washed his head, then poured over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. I handed him a cloth, and he said with his hand like this, and did not want it.”
266.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured with his right hand onto his left in the bath.” Maymūna describes the sequence of the bath. The narrator Sulaymān (al-Aʿmash) says he does not know whether a third time was mentioned, and it remains open whether the hand was rubbed on the ground or on the wall. At the end the Prophet declines the offered cloth with a gesture of his hand.

267.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, he said: “I mentioned him to ʿĀʾisha, and she said: May Allah have mercy on Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān! I used to perfume the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then he would go round his wives, then in the morning he was in iḥrām, with scent streaming from him.”
267.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When one has intercourse and repeats it, and one who went round his wives with a single bath.” ʿĀʾisha responds to the mention of a statement and reports that she perfumed the Prophet, he then went to his wives and in the morning was in iḥrām, with scent streaming from him. The following hadith 270 gives the statement of Ibn ʿUmar to which she refers.

268.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Qatāda, he said: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go round his wives in a single hour of night and day, and they were eleven.” He said: I said to Anas: “Was he able to?” He said: “We used to say that he had been given the strength of thirty.” And Saʿīd said, from Qatāda: Anas narrated to them about nine women.
268.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Anas reports that the Prophet went round his wives in one hour of night or day, eleven in number; asked whether he was able to, Anas gives what was said: he had been given the strength of thirty. A narration by Saʿīd through Qatāda mentions nine women instead of eleven; the text does not explain the difference.

269.matn: Abū l-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Zāʾida narrated to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: “I was a man who discharged a lot of madhy. So I told a man to ask the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, because of the position of his daughter. He asked, and the Prophet said: Perform ablution and wash your male organ.”
269.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing off madhy and ablution because of it.” Because of his relation to the Prophet’s daughter, ʿAlī has another man ask. The Prophet’s answer is: perform ablution and wash the male organ. The text does not name the man who asked.

270.matn: Abū n-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, he said: “I asked ʿĀʾisha and mentioned to her the statement of Ibn ʿUmar: I would not like to be in iḥrām in the morning with scent streaming from me. ʿĀʾisha said: I perfumed the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then he went round among his wives, then in the morning he was in iḥrām.”
270.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who perfumed himself, then bathed, and the trace of perfume remained.” The narrator mentions to ʿĀʾisha the statement of Ibn ʿUmar that he would not like to be in iḥrām with scent streaming from him. ʿĀʾisha replies that she perfumed the Prophet; he then went to his wives and in the morning was in iḥrām.

271.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “It is as if I see the gleam of perfume in the parting of the Prophet’s hair, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in iḥrām.”
271.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter, “One who perfumed himself, then bathed, and the trace of perfume remained.” ʿĀʾisha describes the gleam of perfume in the parting of the Prophet’s hair while he was in iḥrām. The chain runs through Ādam, Shuʿba, al-Ḥakam, Ibrāhīm and al-Aswad to ʿĀʾisha.

272.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, he said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he washed his hands and performed his ablution as for prayer, then he bathed, then he ran his hand through his hair, until, when he thought he had moistened his skin, he poured water over it three times, then he washed the rest of his body.”
272.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Running the fingers through the hair until one thinks the skin is moistened, then pouring water over it.” ʿĀʾisha describes the Prophet’s bath from janāba: first the hands, then the ablution, then running his hand through the hair, then pouring three times and washing the rest of the body.

273.matn: And she said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, scooping from it together.”
273.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith is in the same chapter and has no chain of its own; it follows the previous hadith of ʿĀʾisha (“And she said”). She reports that she and the Prophet bathed from one vessel and scooped from it together.

274.matn: Yūsuf ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, he said: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim, from Kurayb, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna, she said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out water for the bath from janāba. He poured with his right on his left two or three times, then washed his private part, then struck his hand on the ground or the wall two or three times, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and forearms, then poured water over his head, then washed his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. She said: I brought him a cloth, but he did not want it, and he began to shake off with his hand.”
274.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who performed ablution in janāba and then washed the rest of his body.” Maymūna describes the bath from janāba: pouring with the right on the left, washing the private part, rubbing the hand on the ground or the wall, rinsing mouth and nose, washing face and forearms, pouring over head and body, and finally washing the feet. The Prophet declines the cloth and shakes the water off with his hand. The number of repetitions is narrated with uncertainty as “two or three.”

275.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Yūnus narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, he said: “The prayer was called and the rows were straightened, standing. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us. When he stood at his place of prayer, he remembered that he was junub, and said to us: Stay where you are. Then he went back and bathed, then came out to us with his head dripping, said the takbīr, and we prayed with him.” ʿAbd al-Aʿlā followed him in this, from Maʿmar, from az-Zuhrī. And al-Awzāʿī narrated it from az-Zuhrī.
275.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When one remembers in the mosque that one is junub: he goes out as he is and does not perform tayammum.” Abū Hurayra reports that after the call to prayer the Prophet noticed at his place that he was junub, had the people wait, bathed, and came back with his head dripping and began the prayer. The remarks at the end, that ʿAbd al-Aʿlā from Maʿmar and al-Awzāʿī from az-Zuhrī narrate the same, are by al-Bukhārī and support the chain.

276.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamza narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Aʿmash, from Sālim, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna said: “I set out bathing water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and screened him with a cloth. He poured on his hands and washed them, then poured with his right on his left and washed his private part, then struck his hand on the ground and wiped it, then washed it, rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and forearms, then poured over his head and let water flow over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet. I handed him a cloth, but he did not take it, and he went off shaking his hands.”
276.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Shaking the hands after bathing from janāba.” Maymūna describes the same bath as in the previous reports. Here the Prophet does not take the cloth offered and goes off shaking his hands, which is the topic of the chapter.

277.matn: Khallād ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṣafiyya bint Shayba, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When one of us was junub, she would take with her hands three times over her head, then she would take with her hand on her right side and with her other hand on her left side.”
277.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who began with the right side of his head in the bath.” ʿĀʾisha describes how she and the women bathed after janāba: three times over the head, then the right and the left side. The text does not specify the quantity or the vessel.

278.matn: Isḥāq ibn Naṣr narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd ar-Razzāq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at one another. But Mūsā used to bathe alone. They said: By Allah, nothing prevents Mūsā from bathing with us except that he has a hernia of the testicles. Once he went to bathe and put his garment on a stone. The stone fled with his garment, and Mūsā went out after it, saying: My garment, O stone! – until the Children of Israel looked at Mūsā and said: By Allah, there is nothing wrong with Mūsā. He took his garment and began to strike the stone.” Abū Hurayra said: “By Allah, there is a scar on the stone from the striking, six or seven, from striking the stone.”
278.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who bathed naked alone in seclusion, and one who covered himself – covering is better.” The Prophet relates that the Children of Israel bathed naked together while Mūsā bathed alone, and that the people suspected him because of it. The story ends with his body being seen without defect. The last sentence about the scar on the stone is the statement of Abū Hurayra.

279.matn: And from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “While Ayyūb was bathing naked, a swarm of golden locusts fell upon him. Ayyūb began to gather them into his garment. His Lord called to him: O Ayyūb, have I not made you independent of what you see? He said: Yes, by Your might, but I am not independent of Your blessing.” And Ibrāhīm narrated it from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “While Ayyūb was bathing naked …”
279.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith is in the same chapter and begins with “And from Abū Hurayra,” so it links in wording to the previous narration. It tells of Ayyūb bathing naked, golden locusts falling upon him, and his answering his Lord’s question by saying he is not independent of His blessing. The second chain at the end is an addition by al-Bukhārī and gives only the beginning of the wording.

280.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Abū n-Naḍr, the freed slave of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh: Abū Murra, the freed slave of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib, told him that he heard Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib say: “I went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the conquest and found him bathing, with Fāṭima screening him. He said: Who is this? I said: I am Umm Hāniʾ.”
280.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Covering oneself when bathing in front of people.” Umm Hāniʾ reports that she found the Prophet bathing in the year of the conquest, with Fāṭima screening him, and that he asked who she was. The text gives no further sequence of the bath.

281.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna, she said: “I screened the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was bathing from janāba. He washed his hands, then poured with his right on his left and washed his private part and what had touched it, then wiped his hand on the wall or the ground, then performed ablution as for prayer except his feet, then poured water over his body, then moved aside and washed his feet.” Abū ʿAwāna and Ibn Fuḍayl followed him in this, regarding the screening.
281.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Covering oneself when bathing in front of people.” Maymūna screens the Prophet during the bath from janāba, whose sequence she describes; he washes his feet only at the end. The note at the end that Abū ʿAwāna and Ibn Fuḍayl also narrate this regarding the screening is by al-Bukhārī.

282.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from Zaynab bint Abī Salama, from Umm Salama, the Mother of the Believers, that she said: “Umm Sulaym, the wife of Abū Ṭalḥa, came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Must a woman bathe if she has a wet dream? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, if she sees the water.”
282.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When a woman has a wet dream.” Umm Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after a wet dream. The answer is: yes, if she sees the water.

283.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Bakr narrated to us, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayra: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, met him on one of the roads of Medina while he was junub. I slipped away from him, went and bathed, then came. He said: Where were you, O Abū Hurayra? He said: I was junub, and I disliked sitting with you while I was not pure. He said: Glory be to Allah! The Muslim does not become impure.”
283.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The sweat of the junub, and that the Muslim does not become impure.” Abū Hurayra avoids the Prophet while in janāba, bathes and returns; to his explanation the Prophet replies that the Muslim does not become impure.
